title: Perf triage: multi-warp kernel switch & CUDA-graph bisect
summary: Deep technical troubleshooting session focused on nondeterministic kernel switches under high-concurrency workloads. We replicated a 95th-percentile latency regression tied to CUDA-graph replay + persistent KV cache interactions on a multi-gpu on-prem cluster. Discussed root-cause hypotheses (warp scheduling, kernel fallback, quantization-induced math paths), proposed microbench experiments, and agreed on an instrumented bisect plan using NVTX, smallstep batch sweeps, and a TRT-LLM vs vLLM comparison under VPC-like network isolation.
next_steps: Marco to provide instrumented cudagraph playback script and nvtx wrapper by 2026-10-23
Priya to run the microbench matrix (batch sizes 1/2/4/8, seq len 64/128) on their staging nodal cluster and share logs by 2026-10-27
Ava to share security & private deployment notes and a short checklist for KMS/NIC isolation by 2026-10-24
Riley to add telemetry hooks into the Redwood agent that dump kernel selection traces and env vars and push to shared S3 by 2026-10-29
action_items: Marco: instrumented cuda-graph replay + nvtx markers; include per-kernel timing CSV - due 2026-10-23
Priya: isolate workload to single tenant VPC and reproduce 95th latency spike - due 2026-10-27
Liam: capture dmesg and nvidia-smi loop during repro window, attach to ticket - due 2026-10-24

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-10-21 15:30 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Silva (Redwood SE), Riley Adams (Redwood Support Eng), Priya Nair (BlueNova ML Infra), Liam O'Connor (BlueNova Platform), Sara Gomez (BlueNova CTO), Tuan Vu (BlueNova SRE)

Summary: (auto) Short triage to go over kernel path instability when running CUDA-graph replay with persistent KV cache under heavy batching.

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll try to keep this focused, Marco and Riley from engineering are here to help dig into the kernel-switch issue you reported. Priya, can you summarize what you saw?
[00:12] Priya: sure, so over the last week on staging we've seen intermittent 95th pct spikes 5x baseline when running our chat stream workload. It seems tied to persistent KV cache enabled plus cudagraph replay. We only hit it when host concurrency > 32, which makes me think it's a multi-warp scheduling thing or some eviction thrash.
[00:27] Marco: got it, do you have the runbook or the exact flags? like are you using single persistent stream or multi-stream cuGraph? sometimes cudagraph replay with a persistent stream plus manual kernel fallback triggers different kernels.
[00:42] Priya: we run replay mode with warmup graphs, persistent=true, kv_cache=true, quantization=4-bit-some (we're using int4 hybrid). We saw the JIT choose different kernels in the log but it's noisy.
[00:58] Liam: also to add, on-prem cluster is NUMA stitched, NVLink across pairs, but not full fabric. We can repro in staging which mirrors prod networking.
[01:12] Riley: okay that definitely helps. One early hypothesis: quantization path selecting a tensor core vs fp16 math kernel under certain batch/seq combos; when that happens, the graph replay may replay a different launch configuration, causing lane fragmentation and then a fallback kernel that increases latency.
[01:29] Sara: is this specific to TRT-LLM or also seen with vLLM stacks? we tried a quick run with the upstream vllm binary and didn't see the same scale of spikes but the configs weren't identical.
[01:42] Marco: good question—vLLM and TRT-LLM have different kernel packing. TRT-LLM often fuses kernels and uses TRT-specific launch params; vLLM tends to use dynamic kernels that avoid cudagraphs in some codepaths. That difference could explain why one repros and the other doesn't. we should test both with identical inputs and disabled fallbacks.
[01:58] Priya: can you clarify disabled fallbacks? where would we flip that?
[02:04] Marco: in our runtime you can set kernel_fallback=off and force the canonical path, or set a debug flag to force the TRT path even if heuristics would choose vLLM-like kernels. we'll share the exact flag names.
[02:17] Ava: quick housekeeping—Priya, do you have the run id that shows the 95th spike? if so please paste to the shared doc after.
[02:24] Priya: yes i put a reference in the ticket,  run-id bn-20261012-03, link in the notes.

[02:40] Topic: microbench plan
[02:45] Marco: propose a microbench matrix: batch sizes [1,2,4,8], seq lengths [32,64,128], concurrency [8,16,32,64]. For each cell we run: (1) TRT-LLM with cudagraph replay, (2) TRT-LLM with cudagraph disabled, (3) vLLM binary with similar flags, (4) Redwood runtime with kernel_fallback=off. Add metadata: quantization=int4 hybrid vs fp16.
[03:07] Priya: ok that looks painful but doable. How long do you expect each cell to take?
[03:12] Marco: short runs, 30s warmup + 90s steady; total about 6-8 minutes per cell. Might be a half-day job for full matrix.
[03:24] Tuan: we can carve out a maintenance window on staging tomorrow if that helps.

[03:40] Topic: instrumentation
[03:42] Riley: crucial part is NVTX and per-kernel timing. We'll provide a wrapper script that replays cudagraphs and injects NVTX ranges before/after launch and also collects per-launch occupancy and time. Also will patch the runtime to dump which kernel name and kernel selector heuristic value was used.
[03:59] Liam: can you also log the exact env var set (CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING etc)? we saw some differences after a system update where someone enabled CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING in a debug cron job.
[04:10] Riley: yep will include env dump.

[04:18] Priya: a bit of background—our on-prem has a NIC offload that sometimes increases latency jitter when pinned, and our infra team suspects the NIC driver interacts with MPI-like memory registration during cudagraph replay. any obvious checks?
[04:32] Marco: interesting. cudagraphs do memory capture and reuse; if the NIC or HBM registration tables get modified between captures, replay may reallocate and trigger different kernels. We should check pmap/dmesg and ensure no dynamic memory reg during the capture window. Also try reproduce with NIC offload disabled for a run.

[04:50] Sara: okay, big picture question: if TRT path is faster but brittle on your infra, is fallback to vLLM acceptable? we care about 99th stability over raw 50th latency.
[04:58] Ava: that's exactly the tradeoff—TRT gives lower median but sometimes tail spikes when graphs replay with certain quant profiles. Our suggested approach is an SLO-driven policy: favor TRT path for low-cost steady traffic and auto-fallback to vLLM-compatible kernel when tail breaches. We'll demo an automated policy once we reproduce.

[05:20] Topic: debugging bisect idea
[05:23] Marco: propose a bisect: instrument the runtime to toggle a single heuristic at a time (e.g., kernel_selector_level). Start with default and then binary-search which heuristics flip before/after the spike. This reduces noise vs full feature toggles.
[05:36] Priya: i like that. can you provide a small harness to flip heuristics at runtime?
[05:40] Marco: yes, we'll add a debug endpoint to flip kernel_selector thresholds live. We'll timestamp when change applied.

[06:00] [06:00] Priya: quick interjection—about quantization, we saw the int4 path had more kernel switches than fp16, likely because the int4 implementation uses different library kernels that sometimes fall back to non-tensorcore kernels for certain shapes.
[06:16] Marco: correct—int4 typically triggers a different packing and may use explicit dequant/requant kernels; those can cause different cudagraph capture patterns. We'll include int4 vs fp16 in the matrix.

[06:30] Topic: sample logs and what to share
[06:33] Riley: please share: full nvtx annotated trace, per-kernel name CSV with start/dur, environment dump, dmesg, nvidia-smi loop, runtime kernel selector trace. Compress and upload to the shared S3 path.
[06:48] Priya: will do. any preference on anonymizing? we can scrub tenant ids.
[06:52] Ava: scrub tenant ids but keep trace ids.

[07:00] Topic: quick triage run live (we attempt repro in call)
[07:05] Priya: launching a quick warmup run now on our small staging shard with batch=4 seq=128 concurrency=32 (should take 3 minutes).
[07:18] [ambient background typing]
[07:40] Priya: warmup done, starting steady now. I'm watching the 95th line.
[07:55] Liam: tail is holding around 120ms so far.
[08:12] Priya: uh there's a spike, 640ms at 7:56 (that's very similar to the earlier incident).
[08:20] Marco: can you upload the nvtx trace chunk around that timestamp? also can you capture which kernel name was selected from the runtime log?
[08:29] Priya: grabbing now, one sec.
[08:40] Priya: ok uploaded nvtx slice and runtime selector gem under trace bn-20261021-quick. Link in chat.
[08:50] Marco: looking at the trace, I see a sudden switch from kernel packer A->B right before the spike and then a cudagraph replay boundary. The packer B is larger launch config and higher register pressure. That maps to the math path change Riley mentioned.
[09:06] Riley: I also see a memcopy that increased by a few ms before the launch, likely pinning related.

[09:20] Topic: root causes and hypotheses list
[09:23] Marco: hypotheses: (1) quantization causes kernel selector to pick a different packing causing register pressure and kernel fallback under high occupancy, (2) cudagraph capture/replay on persistent streams interacts poorly with NIC memory reg leading to occasional memcpy stalls, (3) NUMA/NVLink topology creates nonuniform prefetch causing eviction and kernel recompile path.
[09:45] Priya: i vote for ordering 1 then 2 based on our hits.

[09:52] Ava: decision: run microbench matrix + bisect with heuristics, capture NVTX and kernel selector traces, then run TRT-LLM vs vLLM head-to-head with identical inputs. If microbench reproduces, we'll trial an SLO-based fallback policy.

[10:10] Topic: constraints on on-prem and VPC
[10:12] Liam: note, security team won't allow us to send raw dmesg out of the cluster to external buckets. we can only share trimmed artifacts with tenant IDs removed.
[10:21] Ava: understood—we'll accept redacted artifacts but need enough to map kernel names and timestamps. We can provide a local script that hashes sensitive fields and keeps necessary telemetry.

[10:32] Priya: also curious—are there perf counters we should not enable in production? we tried enabling a hardware counter and saw jitter increase.
[10:40] Marco: avoid heavy sampling profilers in steady traffic; prefer NVTX micro ranges and per-launch timers which are lightweight. We'll share a minimal tracer.

[10:50] Topic: what success looks like
[10:52] Sara: for us success is deterministic reproduction in staging + a mitigation (config toggles or fallback) that eliminates the 95th spike for 2 weeks under realistic load. We prefer a config over code change if possible.
[11:05] Ava: noted—primary goal is config-based mitigation + clear rollback. If config insufficient we'll move to runtime patch.

[11:12] Closing and recap
[11:14] Ava: recap—Marco sends instrumented playback script and debug toggle endpoint; Priya runs the microbench; Riley provides tracer and runtime selector dumps; everyone uploads artifacts to the shared path; meet in one week for follow-up.
[11:28] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the quick depth here.
[11:35] Marco: thanks, will follow up with exact flags.
[11:40] Ava: ok we'll wrap. bye.

End of transcript.
